LanguageData.SH_Rec1: 12 months, real holidays with moods, parties and gifts
LanguageData.SH_Rec2: Weather by month and three new weathers
LanguageData.SH_Rec3: Birthdays, seasonal moods, traditions and a calendar tab
LanguageData.SH_YearMode_Desc: Which year the colony starts in. The game counts from 5500; you can also play from year 0 or year 1. Only the shown number changes.
LanguageData.SH_CalendarDate_Desc: The date in the corner (and everywhere else) shows the day and month, e.g. "December 4" instead of "4th of Decembary".
LanguageData.SH_SeasonTips_Desc: A letter when winter is coming (harvest, warm clothes, heating) and when the growing season starts.
LanguageData.SH_Holidays_Desc: Real holidays (Czech and international) give the colonists a good mood.
LanguageData.SH_Parties_Desc: A party in the evening of some holidays and on birthdays.
LanguageData.SH_Gifts_Desc: St. Nicholas, Christmas and Children's Day bring gifts in a drop pod (sweets, cookies, silver, medicine, beer).
LanguageData.SH_Events_Desc: Fireworks on New Year's Eve, fog on Halloween night, a chance of a white Christmas.
LanguageData.SH_Letters_Desc: A letter on the morning of a holiday. Off: only a short message.
LanguageData.SH_Birthdays_Desc: A colonist's birthday gives a good mood and often a party.
LanguageData.SH_Traditions_Desc: A holiday celebrated again next year becomes a tradition and gives a bit more mood (up to 3 years).
LanguageData.SH_RealDate_Desc: Holidays come on the real date of your computer (Christmas on the real 24th of December, Easter by the real Easter) instead of the game calendar. Just for fun.
LanguageData.SH_MonthWeather_Desc: More snow in January, showers in April, storms in July, fog in November … The biome's own weather stays, only the chances change.
LanguageData.SH_NewWeathers_Desc: Hoarfrost, Indian summer, spring showers and, where the climate fits, aurora, blizzard, freezing rain, hailstorm, heat haze, sandstorm and monsoon rain.
LanguageData.SH_SeasonalMoods_Desc: First snow, spring in the air, warm summer evenings.
LanguageData.SH_WinterBlues_Desc: A small bad mood in the darkest month of winter.
LanguageData.SH_HD_NewYear: A new year begins: a celebration, and every colonist makes a resolution (learns faster for 5 days).
LanguageData.SH_HL_NewYear: Happy New Year! The colony celebrates the start of a new year. Everyone made a resolution to learn more – for a few days they learn faster. There is a party in the evening.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Valentine: Valentine's Day! Couples spend the day together a little closer than usual.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Carnival: Masks, music and a feast before the lean weeks; a party.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Carnival: Masopust! Masks, music and a big feast. There is a party in the afternoon.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Easter: Painted eggs and spring – everyone gets a good mood.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Easter: Happy Easter! Painted eggs, spring flowers and a good mood everywhere.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Witches: A big bonfire in the evening to chase the winter away; a party.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Witches: Witches' Night! Tonight we burn the witch and chase the winter away. There is a party in the evening.
LanguageData.SH_HD_MayDay: Couples kiss under a blossoming tree.
LanguageData.SH_HL_MayDay: The first of May – the time of love. Couples kiss under a blossoming tree.
LanguageData.SH_HD_ChildrenDay: Children get a great mood and sweets; adults enjoy their joy.
LanguageData.SH_HL_ChildrenDay: Children's Day! Today is all about the kids – games and sweets.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Solstice: The longest day of the year, celebrated outside; a party.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Solstice: Midsummer – the longest day of the year. There is a party in the evening under the open sky.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Harvest: A feast for the harvest – the fuller the stores, the better the mood; a party.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Harvest: Dožínky – the harvest festival! The colony celebrates the harvest. The more food in the stores, the better the mood. There is a party in the afternoon.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Halloween: Pumpkins and spooky stories; fog in the evening.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Halloween: Happy Halloween! Pumpkins, spooky stories … and tonight the fog rolls in. Boo!
LanguageData.SH_HD_AllSouls: Remembering the dead – the grief for those who died becomes easier.
LanguageData.SH_HL_AllSouls: All Souls' Day. The colony remembers those who are no longer here. Remembering together makes the grief easier.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Thanksgiving: A feast of thanks; a party.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Thanksgiving: Thanksgiving! Time to be thankful for what we have – and for each other. There is a feast in the afternoon.
LanguageData.SH_HD_StNicholas: St. Nicholas brings sweets – the children are thrilled.
LanguageData.SH_HL_StNicholas: St. Nicholas came with an angel and a devil! Good children get sweets – the naughty ones a lump of coal. (Just kidding, everyone gets chocolate.)
LanguageData.SH_HD_Christmas: Christmas Eve: gifts, cookies, a feast and the best mood of the year; maybe a white Christmas.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Christmas: Merry Christmas! Gifts have arrived – Christmas cookies and more. In the evening the whole colony meets for the Christmas Eve feast.
LanguageData.SH_HD_NewYearsEve: A party in the evening and fireworks before midnight.
LanguageData.SH_HL_NewYearsEve: New Year's Eve! The party starts in the evening, and before midnight the fireworks light up the sky.
LanguageData.SH_GiftChildren: Gifts for the children have arrived!
LanguageData.SH_BirthdayMsg: {0} has a birthday today ({1})! Happy birthday!
LanguageData.SH_FirstSnowMsg: The first snow of the year!
LanguageData.SH_TipWinter:
{0} is near and it will be cold (about {1}).

- Harvest the fields before the frost.
- Make warm clothes (parkas, tuques).
- Prepare heating and fuel.
- Store enough food for the winter.
LanguageData.SH_TipSpring: In {0} it will be warm enough for the plants. Time to sow the fields!
LanguageData.SH_TraditionNote: The colony has celebrated this holiday {0} times – it is our tradition now.
LanguageData.SH_YearDays_Desc: How many days one year has. 60 is the game's own year (12 months of 5 days). With a longer year the seasons, the date and the seasonal temperature run slower – a 365-day year has real months and a winter of about three months, so plan your food. Day and night stay the same. Changing it in a running game keeps today's season.
LanguageData.SH_AgeWithYear: Colonists age with the calendar year
LanguageData.SH_AgeWithYear_Desc: On: a colonist grows one year older per calendar year, so with a 365-day year people (and children) age about six times slower than in the game. Off: everybody ages as in the game (one year per 60 days) – several birthdays a calendar year.
LanguageData.SH_PackAsia_Desc: Lunar New Year, Holi, Diwali and the Mid-Autumn Festival – mood, a party and fireworks.
LanguageData.SH_PackAmericas_Desc: Day of the Dead and Founders' Day (with fireworks).
LanguageData.SH_PackEurope_Desc: St. Patrick's Day, Oktoberfest (both with a little beer) and St. Martin's Day.
LanguageData.SH_PackDays_Desc: Pi Day, Earth Day, Book Day, Towel Day, Chocolate Day, Cat Day, Talk Like a Pirate Day, Smile Day – only a short message, no mood.
LanguageData.SH_PlantColors: Plants change colour with the seasons
LanguageData.SH_PlantColors_Desc: Looks only: leafy trees turn yellow, orange and red in autumn and bare in winter, conifers stay green, wild grass turns straw-coloured. Growth, temperatures, raids and traders are not affected. In the tropics nothing changes.
LanguageData.SH_GiftBeer: A few bottles of beer arrived for the evening.
LanguageData.SH_HD_LunarNewYear: Red lanterns, a feast and fireworks for a lucky year.
LanguageData.SH_HL_LunarNewYear: Happy Lunar New Year! Red lanterns hang everywhere and tonight there will be fireworks.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Holi: The festival of colours: everyone throws coloured powder at everyone.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Holi: Holi! The festival of colours – in the afternoon the colony celebrates and nobody stays clean.
LanguageData.SH_HD_Diwali: The festival of lights: lamps in the windows and fireworks.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Diwali: Happy Diwali! Lamps are lit in every window, and tonight fireworks light the sky.
LanguageData.SH_HL_MidAutumn: The Mid-Autumn Festival – in the evening everyone gathers to look at the moon.
LanguageData.SH_HD_DayOfDead: Candles, marigolds and stories of the dead; the grief for them eases.
LanguageData.SH_HL_DayOfDead: Día de Muertos – the colony remembers its dead with candles and flowers. It is a day of memories, not of sorrow.
LanguageData.SH_HD_FoundersDay: A celebration of how it all began, with fireworks in the evening.
LanguageData.SH_HL_FoundersDay: Founders' Day! A party in the afternoon and fireworks at night.
LanguageData.SH_HD_StPatrick: Everything green, songs and a pint or two.
LanguageData.SH_HL_StPatrick: Happy St. Patrick's Day! Wear something green – there is beer for the evening.
LanguageData.SH_HL_Oktoberfest: O'zapft is! Oktoberfest starts – beer has arrived and the party starts in the afternoon.
LanguageData.SH_HL_StMartin: St. Martin came on a white horse! Roast goose for dinner.
LanguageData.SH_HL_PiDay: 3.14159… someone baked a pie in honour of the occasion.
LanguageData.SH_HL_EarthDay: Earth Day – a good day to plant a tree.
LanguageData.SH_HL_BookDay: World Book Day – someone dusted off an old book tonight.
LanguageData.SH_HL_TowelDay: Towel Day – don't panic, and know where your towel is.
LanguageData.SH_HL_ChocolateDay: Chocolate Day – if there is any chocolate left, today is the day.
LanguageData.SH_HL_CatDay: International Cat Day – the cats act as if every day was theirs anyway.
LanguageData.SH_HL_PirateDay: Arr, matey! Today everyone talks like a pirate.
LanguageData.SH_HL_SmileDay: World Smile Day – a smile costs nothing.
LanguageData.SH_Activities_Desc: On a holiday morning a letter offers something to do – an egg hunt, a witch bonfire, a maypole, carols … – and the colonists do it themselves. A few happen by themselves (New Year's resolutions, grave candles, St. Nicholas).
LanguageData.SH_HolidayTrader_Desc: At Christmas and Easter a friendly caravan brings seasonal goods: cookies, chocolate, painted eggs, toys, beer and fine meals.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_NewYear: Every colonist picks one skill (a passion, or his weakest skill) and learns it 50% faster for a season.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Valentine: Couples get a romantic dinner (a big mood) and romance is more likely all day.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Carnival: A costume parade with a party; the next day a short fast.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Easter: Painted eggs are hidden around the colony. Haulers find them and colonists eat them for fun.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Witches: A bonfire with a straw witch; the colony gathers around it.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_MayDay: A maypole is raised. Keep somebody near it on the night after, or the neighbours may steal it. Couples kiss under a blooming tree.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_ChildrenDay: Children get toys. With no children the rest of the day is a day off for everyone.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Solstice: Medicinal herbs give 50% more today, and a fire is lit by the water.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Harvest: A harvest wreath and a feast; crops give 25% more today.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Halloween: Pumpkin lanterns light up the colony and the neighbours' kids come trick-or-treating – sweets from your storage raise goodwill. Sometimes a (harmless) ghost is seen at night.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_AllSouls: A candle is lit beside every grave.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Thanksgiving: A big feast, and a friendly faction sends food.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_StNicholas: Good colonists get a gift, the naughty ones (a recent mental break, prisoners) a lump of coal.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Christmas: Carols at the Christmas tree (build one under Misc). On Christmas morning the presents lie under the tree.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_NewYearsEve: The countdown party and fireworks; the next morning some colonists have a hangover.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Valentine: It's Valentine's Day! Shall we prepare a romantic dinner for the couples? Love will be in the air all day.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Carnival: It's Carnival! Masks on – shall we hold a costume parade with a feast? (Tomorrow comes the fast.)
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Easter: Happy Easter! Shall we hide painted eggs around the colony? Haulers will find them and everyone gets to eat them.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Witches: It's Witches' Night! Shall we build a bonfire with a straw witch and chase the winter away?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_MayDay: It's the first of May! Shall we raise a maypole? But beware – the neighbours like to steal it at night. Keep someone awake near it the night after.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_ChildrenDay: It's Children's Day! Shall we celebrate? Children get toys – and if there are no children, everyone gets the rest of the day off.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Solstice: It's Midsummer! Herbs gathered today are twice as strong, they say. Shall we light a fire by the water?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Harvest: The harvest festival! Shall we hang a harvest wreath and hold a feast? Crops harvested today give more.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Halloween: It's Halloween! Shall we light pumpkin lanterns and welcome the neighbours' kids for trick-or-treat? Have some sweets in storage!
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Thanksgiving: It's Thanksgiving! Shall we sit down to a big feast? Perhaps the neighbours will send something too.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Christmas: Merry Christmas! Shall we sing carols around the Christmas tree?
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Valentine: Candles, flowers and a nice dinner for {N} couples. Love is in the air all day.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Carnival: Masks, music and doughnuts – the colony parades in costume. Tomorrow the fast begins.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Easter: {N} painted eggs are hidden around the colony. Haulers will find them – and everyone may eat them for fun.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Witches: The bonfire with the straw witch is lit! The colony gathers around it to chase the winter away.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_MayDay: The maypole stands! Keep someone awake or drafted near it the night after – the neighbours like to steal it.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_MaypoleStolen: In the night, people from {FACTION} sneaked in and stole our maypole! It's an old custom – no harm done, but next year we guard it better.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_ChildrenDay: Toys for {N} children! Today is all about them.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_ChildrenDayOff: No children here – so the rest of today is a day off for everyone. The schedules come back at midnight.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Solstice: The midsummer fire is lit. Medicinal herbs harvested today give 50% more.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Harvest: The harvest wreath hangs and the feast begins. Crops harvested today give 25% more.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Halloween: {0} pumpkin lanterns grin into the night.
LanguageData.SH_TreatsGiven: Kids from {1} came trick-or-treating and got {0} sweets from our storage. Their parents are pleased.
LanguageData.SH_NoTreats: Kids from {0} came trick-or-treating, but we had no sweets in storage. Maybe next year.
LanguageData.SH_Ghost: {0} swears something white floated past the window tonight… Spooky, but a great story.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Thanksgiving: A long table full of food. {FACTION} sent a gift for the feast.
LanguageData.SH_ActDoneTitle_StNicholas: St. Nicholas, the angel and the devil
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_StNicholas:
St. Nicholas came with an angel and a devil!

Good this year: {GOOD} – a gift for each.
Naughty: {BAD} – the devil left coal.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Christmas: The colony gathers at the Christmas tree to sing carols.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_ChristmasNoTree: The colony gathers to sing carols. Next year build a Christmas tree (Misc) – the presents will lie under it.
LanguageData.SH_GiftUnderTree: The Christmas presents are under the tree!
LanguageData.SH_Rec4: Holiday food and decorations, seasonal events, holidays by your colony's culture
LanguageData.SH_HD_SpringEquinox: Day and night are equal: the old festival of sowing. Celebrated by tribal colonies.
LanguageData.SH_HL_SpringEquinox: Day and night are equal today. The tribe blesses the fields for a good year.
LanguageData.SH_HD_WinterSolstice: The longest night of the year: a big fire to call the sun back. Celebrated by tribal colonies.
LanguageData.SH_HL_WinterSolstice: The longest night of the year. Tonight the tribe keeps a big fire burning – from tomorrow the sun comes back.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_LunarNewYear: Happy Lunar New Year! Shall we hang red lanterns and give each other red envelopes with a little silver?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Holi: Happy Holi! A colour fight? Everyone will be colourful for half a day – and the clothes a little stained.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Diwali: Happy Diwali! Shall we light little lamps around the colony tonight and share sweets?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_MidAutumn: The Mid-Autumn Festival! Tonight mooncakes and watching the full moon together?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_DayOfDead: The Day of the Dead. Shall we build an altar and remember those we lost?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_FoundersDay: Founders' Day! Our best speaker gives a speech, then a feast?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_StPatrick: St. Patrick's Day! A green party with songs and dancing?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_Oktoberfest: Oktoberfest! A beer contest? Every contestant needs one beer from our storage.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_StMartin: St. Martin's Day! A lantern walk tonight and a goose dinner? The goose takes some raw meat from the storage.
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_SpringEquinox: The spring equinox. Shall the tribe bless the fields with a wreath and a dance?
LanguageData.SH_ActOffer_WinterSolstice: Yule, the longest night. Shall we light a big fire tonight and keep it burning?
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_LunarNewYear: Red lanterns around the colony; every colonist gives a red envelope with a little silver to another one.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Holi: A colour fight: everyone is colourful for half a day, the clothes get a little stained.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Diwali: Little oil lamps around the colony and sweets for everybody (in the evening).
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_MidAutumn: Mooncakes and watching the moon together outside (in the evening).
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_DayOfDead: An altar of the dead; every colonist remembers one of the colony's dead by name.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_FoundersDay: The colonist with the best Social skill gives a speech – the better the speaker, the better the mood. Then a feast.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_StPatrick: A green party with songs and dancing.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_Oktoberfest: A beer contest – one beer from the storage per contestant; the winner is proud for days.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_StMartin: A lantern walk in the evening; with raw meat in the storage also a goose dinner.
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_SpringEquinox: A wreath and a dance to bless the fields (tribal colonies).
LanguageData.SH_ActDesc_WinterSolstice: A big fire through the longest night (tribal colonies, in the evening).
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_LunarNewYear: Red lanterns glow around the colony and the red envelopes go round:\n\n{LIST}
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Holi: Pink, green, yellow, blue – nobody stays clean! Everyone is colourful until tomorrow, and the clothes got a little stained.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Diwali: {N} little lamps are burning around the colony, and there are sweets for everybody.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_MidAutumn: Mooncakes for everybody, and the colony gathers outside to watch the moon.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_DayOfDead: Marigolds, candles and photos on the altar. Today we remember: {LIST}.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_DayOfDeadNone: The altar stands with marigolds and candles. Luckily, our colony has not lost anyone yet.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_FoundersDay: {PAWN} gave a speech about our {DAYS} days here. {HOW} Then the feast began.
LanguageData.SH_SpeechQ0: It was a bit long, to be honest.
LanguageData.SH_SpeechQ2: A moving speech – there were tears.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_StPatrick: Everything is green today – songs, dancing and a pint in hand.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_Oktoberfest: {N} contestants, {N} beers, brass music – and the winner is {PAWN}! Prost!
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_OktoberfestNoBeer: No beer contest this year – we need at least two contestants and one beer each in the storage ({N} contestants).
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_StMartin: A lantern walk in the dark, then roast goose for everybody. Martin came on a white horse!
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_StMartinNoGoose: A lantern walk in the dark. There was not enough raw meat in the storage for a goose – maybe next year.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_SpringEquinox: The tribe hangs a wreath and dances around the fields for a good harvest.
LanguageData.SH_ActDone_WinterSolstice: The big fire is lit. Tonight we keep it burning – the sun will come back.
LanguageData.SH_ActQuiet: {0}: {1} – start it in the calendar (▶) if you want.
LanguageData.SH_LookingForwardMsg: {0} colonists are looking forward to {1} – they enjoyed it last year.
LanguageData.SH_Visitors: Friends from {0} came to celebrate {1} with us and brought gifts.
LanguageData.SH_PackAwayHint: The season is over: {0} holiday decorations could be packed away (uninstall them).
LanguageData.SH_PackAwayMarked: The season is over: {0} holiday decorations are marked to be packed away.
LanguageData.SH_Thaw: The snow is melting. For the next two days the ground by the water is soft mud – colonists walk slower near water.
LanguageData.SH_MarketMsg: A harvest market caravan from {0} is coming with lots of food.
LanguageData.SH_RemindDays_Desc: A short message this many days before a holiday.
LanguageData.SH_QuietMode_Desc: Holidays and activities only as short messages, no letters. Activities can still be started in the calendar (▶).
LanguageData.SH_HolidayVisitors_Desc: Now and then friendly neighbours come to celebrate a holiday with you and bring gifts (at most every 15 days).
LanguageData.SH_CultureMode_Desc: Auto: a tribal colony keeps the old festivals (equinox, Yule) and skips the modern ones (Founders' Day, Oktoberfest …); other colonies the other way round. All: every holiday, the list below is ignored. My list: only the list below.
LanguageData.SH_LookForward_Desc: Colonists who enjoyed a holiday last year look forward to it a few days before.
LanguageData.SH_FamilyTradition_Desc: More mood when a holiday is celebrated together with a partner, a parent or a child – more every year.
LanguageData.SH_SeasonalFood_Desc: Holiday food (Easter eggs, cookies, mulled wine, pumpkin pie, punch, mooncakes, Diwali sweets) gives extra mood when eaten in its season. The recipes are always available at the stove.
LanguageData.SH_PackAway_Desc: Christmas tree, wreath, light garland, carved pumpkin and maypole (Misc tab) belong to a season. After it: nothing, a reminder, or mark them to be packed away (uninstalled).
LanguageData.SH_SeasonalEvents_Desc: Small events of the year: spring thaw, autumn harvest market, cozy winter evenings, summer insects.
LanguageData.SH_SpringThaw_Desc: After a frosty winter the first days of spring can be wet: two days of mud by the water (colonists walk a bit slower there).
LanguageData.SH_HarvestMarket_Desc: In autumn a friendly caravan often comes with lots of food to sell.
LanguageData.SH_CozyEvenings_Desc: In winter evenings colonists near a lit fireplace or campfire in the same room get a small mood bonus.
LanguageData.SH_SummerInsects_Desc: In hot humid places colonists outdoors in summer are annoyed by mosquitoes (small bad mood).
LanguageData.SH_MoodN_Desc: How strong the holiday mood is. Click to change: 0 %, 50 %, 100 %, 150 %, 200 %.
LanguageData.SH_DayPartyNo: Not possible right now (the colonist is away, busy, or a party is already on).
LanguageData.MUI_DescOn: The mod sets itself up and works right away. Ideal for new players and anyone who does not want to tweak anything.
LanguageData.MUI_DescOffSame: Custom settings. Still the same as recommended.
LanguageData.MUI_ConfirmOn: Turn recommended settings on? Your changes ({0}) will be replaced with the recommended values.
LanguageData.MUI_Locked: Detailed settings are locked. Want to change them? Turn off the switch above – your values start from the recommended ones.
LanguageData.MUI_ChangedTip: Differs from the recommended setting ({0}). Click to restore the recommended value.
